title: Fluoride treatment
what: The dentist puts a varnish or gel with fluoride on your teeth. It strengthens the enamel and protects against tooth decay.
why: For children, to prevent tooth decay; for adults with sensitive teeth or a high risk of decay; and after a dental cleaning.
tell_doctor: If your child has any teeth that hurt
If you use fluoride toothpaste at home

prepare.title: Before the visit
prepare.text: Brush your teeth. Fluoride is often applied right after a professional cleaning.

prepare.title: Food
prepare.text: Eat beforehand. You cannot eat for a while after the treatment.

bring: Your child's ID, if the treatment is for a child
steps: Plaque is cleaned off the teeth
The teeth are dried with air
The varnish is brushed on, or a tray with gel is put in
After a few minutes, the tray is removed. Varnish stays on the teeth
feel: The varnish may feel sticky and have its own taste
after: Usually do not eat or drink for 1 to 2 hours. Ask your dentist
On the day, do not brush your teeth until the evening, or as your dentist says
It is usually repeated every 3 to 6 months

faq.q: Is it harmful for my child?
faq.a: No. Dentists use a dose that is safe for children. Your child is asked not to swallow the gel.

faq.q: How often is fluoride treatment needed?
faq.a: Usually 2 to 4 times a year. Your dentist will decide based on the risk of decay.

reminders.text: Fluoride treatment soon. Brush your teeth and eat beforehand.
